title: Bilal ibn Rabah
summary: From enslaved outcast to the first voice of the adhan.
body: Bilal ibn Rabah was an Abyssinian man enslaved in Makkah when he accepted Islam in its earliest years. His enslaver, Umayyah ibn Khalaf, tortured him in the desert heat for refusing to renounce his faith, but Bilal is remembered for repeating only one word through his suffering: "Ahad" — One, in reference to the oneness of God. He was eventually freed after Abu Bakr purchased his liberty. Bilal went on to become one of the closest companions of the Prophet ﷺ and, because of his powerful voice, was chosen as the first person to call the adhan, the call to prayer — a role that placed a man once treated as the lowest in Makkan society at the very center of the young Muslim community's daily life.
reference: Recorded across the earliest seerah and hadith literature; his endurance under persecution is among the most frequently cited episodes of the early Makkan period.
